reference_sql:
SELECT a.variant, COUNT(*) AS quick_conversions
FROM ab_assignments a
JOIN ab_conversions c
  ON c.test_id = a.test_id
 AND c.customer_id = a.customer_id
WHERE c.converted_at >= a.assigned_at
  AND c.converted_at <= a.assigned_at + INTERVAL 60 MINUTE
GROUP BY a.variant
alternatives: SELECT a.variant, COUNT(*) AS quick_conversions FROM ab_assignments a JOIN ab_conversions c ON c.test_id = a.test_id AND c.customer_id = a.customer_id WHERE c.converted_at BETWEEN a.assigned_at AND a.assigned_at + INTERVAL 1 HOUR GROUP BY a.variant

SELECT a.variant, COUNT(*) AS quick_conversions FROM ab_assignments a JOIN ab_conversions c ON c.test_id = a.test_id AND c.customer_id = a.customer_id WHERE date_diff('second', a.assigned_at, c.converted_at) BETWEEN 0 AND 3600 GROUP BY a.variant

other_way.sql: SELECT a.variant, COUNT(*) AS quick_conversions FROM ab_assignments a JOIN ab_conversions c ON c.test_id = a.test_id AND c.customer_id = a.customer_id WHERE date_diff('second', a.assigned_at, c.converted_at) BETWEEN 0 AND 3600 GROUP BY a.variant
other_way.tradeoff: Counting seconds with date_diff('second', ...) is exact here, while date_diff('hour', ...) would count clock hours, not 60 minutes.

solver.query:
SELECT a.variant, COUNT(*) AS quick_conversions
FROM ab_conversions c
JOIN ab_assignments a ON a.test_id = c.test_id AND a.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE CAST(c.converted_at AS TIMESTAMP) >= CAST(a.assigned_at AS TIMESTAMP)
  AND CAST(c.converted_at AS TIMESTAMP) <= CAST(a.assigned_at AS TIMESTAMP) + INTERVAL 60 MINUTE
GROUP BY a.variant
